auditor_value: Plank: weight at its centre, ground normal and ground friction at the lower end, cylinder's normal perpendicular to the plank at the contact. Cylinder: weight at centre, plank's normal (perpendicular to plank, through the centre), ground normal (vertical, through centre), ground friction (horizontal, at the ground contact).

findings.quote: The cylinder touches the rough ground, so at that contact a normal reaction (vertical, through the centre) and a friction force (horizontal, along the ground) act; the friction is needed because the plank's normal force on the cylinder has a horizontal component.
findings.note: Step 4 (index 3) already lists all four forces on the cylinder with the same directions, including the ground normal and ground friction; this step repeats those two forces under different symbols (N_ground2 vs N_ground,cyl). Duplicated prose.
findings.fix: Merge into the previous step: keep the four-force list once, and add the single sentence explaining why ground friction is drawn (the plank's push has a horizontal component).

notes: Force lists match mine. The why_this_step remark that ground friction is the only force with a moment about the cylinder's centre, so the cylinder cannot stay at rest, is true (with zero friction the horizontal part of the plank's push is unbalanced instead). Drawing ground friction on the cylinder is the standard FBD answer.
